title: India firm on 'energy drink' crackdown despite Pepsi, Red Bull, Monster protest- Moneycontrol.com
summary: India's food regulator has ordered makers of high-caffeine beverages sold as "energy drinks" to stop using that description, prompting a standoff with major brands. Regulators say claims of vitalizing the body or aiding weakness are misleading and have given companies 90 days to comply. Industry groups urged more consultation, while health concerns over high caffeine and sugar persist globally.
content:
India has ordered makers of high-caffeine beverages sold as "energy drinks" to stop using that description, rejecting efforts to stall the regulatory intervention in a fast-growing market expected to be worth $1.6 billion by 2028.

The country's food safety regulator said on social media in early July it had issued notices to companies saying there were no Indian standards for such products and that claims a beverage "vitalizes body and mind" or can "aid in general weakness" were misleading. The regulator gave no further details at the time.

The move has triggered a standoff with companies, who fear removing the category label could damage brands built around instant-energy claims and disrupt sales. At a closed-door meeting with senior industry executives, FSSAI Chief Executive Rajit Punhani rejected arguments over the business impact, saying companies were free to challenge the decision in court.

According to an Indian government source, the industry agreed to comply with the labelling change after the discussion, and the regulator has given companies 90 days to implement the new labelling requirements.

Energy drinks have drawn health concerns in several jurisdictions because they can contain high levels of caffeine, sugar and additives such as taurine. For example, high-caffeine energy drinks will be banned for under-16s in England from April next year, and some regions in Pakistan require they be called "stimulant drinks".

The energy drinks business is heavily built on instant-energy marketing. Red Bull's "Gives You Wings" slogan is globally famous, while Pepsi markets its Sting energy drink in India with ads that portray it as delivering "electrifying energy." Companies worry that removing the "energy drink" label will undermine these brand messages.

The Indian Beverage Association, representing major manufacturers, said it is committed to complying with regulations and engaging constructively with regulators on science-based policy. In a confidential July 6 letter to the regulator, the association warned that public disclosure of preliminary notices could damage reputations, disrupt operations and confuse consumers, and urged a "risk-based enforcement approach." It called for regular stakeholder consultations and a predictable, consultative and transparent framework to reduce litigation and facilitate smoother compliance.

Reuters reported the lobbying efforts and India's decision. Regulators and company executives did not provide further public comment; Pepsi declined to comment and other companies did not respond to requests. The development marks a notable regulatory push into a category that has expanded quickly in India and attracted scrutiny elsewhere for potential health impacts.

Observers say the outcome could reshape marketing and labelling practices in India's beverage sector and may prompt similar regulatory scrutiny in other markets where energy drinks are popular.

(Reporting based on material from Moneycontrol and Reuters coverage of industry and regulatory responses.)
